refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement concludes “Then $k_x$ is Schwartz,” and Proof 1.1 refers to “Schwartz seminorms,” but the item neither states nor identifies the definition. The published supplier `def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms` defines this by finiteness of every $p_{\alpha,\beta}(f)=\sup_x|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$. The item does not include that definition among its dependencies or state the criterion, leaving this technical conclusion insufficiently specified.

The limit is written using $k_{x,1}^j(dg_x^{-1}v,v)$. Neither this item nor its supplier defines $k_{x,1}^j$ or this two-point notation. `lem-equivariant-rescaled-heat-kernel-extension` defines $k_x(w)$ and states the two-point rescaling limit as $k_x(a-b)$, so the displayed integrand is not defined as written; it can be expressed using the fiber kernel at $dg_x^{-1}v-v$.

`def-equivariant-elliptic-complex-index` defines ellipticity by exactness of the principal-symbol sequence at every nonzero cotangent vector. Verification 1.1 computes the de Rham cohomology and then applies the index definition, but does not establish that exactness. For the de Rham complex the symbol is $i\xi\wedge$, contracted by $(i|\xi|^2)^{-1}\iota_{\xi^\sharp}$ when $\xi\ne0$; this closes the gap immediately, but the check is absent.
